title: Cozmo stack source-fidelity manifest
about: One record per behaviour-affecting decision, or tightly bound group of decisions, in the hand-written
production code of cozmo-stack. Platform plumbing that cannot change what the robot does (logging,
collection choices, string formatting, file layout) is not recorded.
The manifest, not the prose documents, is the authoritative statement of what rests on primary source.
re-analysis/tools/fidelity.py validates it and regenerates FIDELITY_GAPS.md from it.

Two further fields are independent of status: a record's verification (capture or hardware agreement, never provenance) and a subsystem's review (whether it has been through the evidence process in AGENTS.md).
authority_order: the decompiled Unity C# (unity/scripts/csharp) and managed assemblies
the shipped Wwise banks, their .txt definition files, SoundbanksInfo.xml and PluginInfo.xml
the shipped OBB assets, configuration and animation data
CLAD / message schemas and the code generated from them
captures taken from the original app (re-analysis/captures)
existing reverse-engineering notes, only after checking them against the primary evidence above

statuses.EXACT_SOURCE: Read from primary source and reproduced. The record names the address, asset or schema it was read from.
statuses.EQUIVALENT_IMPLEMENTATION: The native behaviour is known from primary source and this stack reaches the same observable effect by a different mechanism. The record names the difference, and the difference has to be one a listener, a viewer or the robot cannot tell apart.
statuses.RECOVERABLE_GAP: A behaviour-affecting decision whose answer plausibly exists in primary source that has not been read, or has been read too shallowly to settle it. The work outstanding is reverse engineering.
statuses.IMPLEMENTATION_GAP: The native behaviour is established from primary evidence, and the production implementation knowingly does something else. The work outstanding is building it. This is unfinished fidelity work, not a policy.
statuses.COMPATIBILITY_POLICY: A deliberate product or platform decision this stack intends to keep: offline tools, the test harness, PC-side plumbing, or a stand-in the operator has to ask for. Not a place to put fidelity work that is hard.
statuses.HARDWARE_ONLY: No shipped artifact can settle it; only a robot, or a recording of the stock app, can.
statuses.BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: The answer lies in third-party code or data that is not in the package (Omron OKAO, the Wwise runtime DSP, the Acapela text-to-speech engine).

verification_levels.NONE: No capture or robot run has been checked against this record. The default when a record carries no verification field.
verification_levels.CAPTURE_VERIFIED: A capture of the original app, or of the robot, agrees with this record. The bundles field names the capture(s).
verification_levels.HARDWARE_VERIFIED: A hardware run of this stack agrees with this record. The bundles field names the run bundle(s). It says the behaviour works, never where it came from.

review_states.UNREVIEWED: The subsystem's records and flags were written before the evidence process in AGENTS.md. Nothing vouches for them.
review_states.INVENTORY_APPROVED: The operator approved an inventory of every behaviour-changing step. Its evidence is frozen in the snapshot until the next approval.
review_states.ACCEPTED: Implemented against the approved inventory, independently verified, and committed as accepted_commit.

gate.rule: Two separate questions, and neither may be answered by the other. A subsystem's source investigation is exhausted only when it holds no RECOVERABLE_GAP on a live execution path; its implementation fidelity is complete only when it holds no IMPLEMENTATION_GAP there. A subsystem can have exhausted the source and still not reproduce what the source says, and neither state means the behaviour is faithfully reproduced: BLOCKED_EXTERNAL and HARDWARE_ONLY items can remain in both cases, and are counted separately so that they cannot be lost behind a single word.

field_notes.location: repository-relative path, optionally with :line, of the code the record is about
field_notes.effect: what a listener, viewer or the robot would observe if this decision were wrong
field_notes.provenance: what the current implementation actually rests on
field_notes.authority: the best available original evidence for this decision
field_notes.evidence: concrete references: native addresses, asset paths, bank object ids, capture files
field_notes.unresolved: for a RECOVERABLE_GAP, what has still to be read; for an IMPLEMENTATION_GAP, what has still to be built; empty string when nothing is
field_notes.hardware_required: whether a robot is genuinely needed to settle it
field_notes.live_path: whether the decision is reached on a normal run against a robot
field_notes.test: the regression that would fail if the recovered behaviour were undone
field_notes.verification: optional; {level, bundles}: whether a capture or a robot run has agreed with the record. Absent means NONE. Never changes status

records.title: The feed: FIFO drain stopping at the first over-budget message; per Update, one 33 ms frame at a time while the drain completes and the audio animation is ready

records.provenance: compared against re-analysis/inventory/M3-device.md on 2026-09-24 and reproduced by the code (M3 batch, verifier fixes B1..B4): StreamSendBuffer.Drain is SendBufferedMessages: FIFO, stopping at the first message over the byte budget or at an audio message with the audio budget 0 (reported, like an emptied buffer, as the engine's 0 result), and at a failed send (the error). AnimationScheduler.Advance is one Update (A13..A20): budgets refreshed, leftovers flushed (a send error ends the Update), then while the buffer is empty and the clip has frames left one frame is built and drained, and the stream time takes its 33 ms step after every drain without a send error, a budget stop included (A18; StreamTimeMs). With no frames left and the buffer empty, EndOfAnimation goes directly when StartOfAnimation was sent; if it never was, AudioSilence and StartOfAnimation are buffered and drained and the end follows on a later Update (A20; that branch is unreachable while this stack's HasFramesLeft rule always builds a frame first). An empty clip completes with nothing sent (A12, A13). A cancel keeps the send buffer, the next Update flushes it within the budget, and no EndOfAnimation follows (A24, A25); a replacement drops it (InitStream's ClearSendBuffer, A12). AbortAnimation 0x8D is not sent (M5, A22/A23). On a production robot the engine tick runs the streamer from Robot::Update while streaming is open (CD12), with no 30 Hz tick loop; the TargetInFlight 10 / 200 ms / priming model is gone. CozmoAudio.Play (policy M3-017) goes through the same buffer and budget.

records.title: Stereo IMA ADPCM: the block is two mono blocks side by side
records.provenance: the seven shipped stereo files, decoded; the layout is arithmetic the files either fit or do not
records.authority: the shipped stereo ADPCM media in Cozmo.bnk - their fmt headers and their data
evidence: The header settles the block. All seven stereo files are 48000 Hz with nAvgBytesPerSec 54000 and nBlockAlign 72, so 750 blocks a second and 64 samples per channel in each. A 36-byte mono block holds exactly 64 samples ((36 - 4) * 2), so a 72-byte stereo block is two of them: the left channel's four-byte header and thirty-two bytes of nibbles, then the right channel's.

The bytes agree. Read that way, all 226 per-channel headers across the seven files (113 blocks each) carry a step index inside the table's 0..88; read as two four-byte headers followed by one run of nibbles, between 50 and 67 of every 226 are out of range. Decoding the seven gives 7232 samples per channel each, peaks of 4430, 18259, 18916, 23387, 25453 and twice full scale, and the two that touch the rails do so 2 and 14 times in 14464 samples - ordinary near-full-scale content, not a decoder running away.

The eight events that reach those files - Play__Robot_SFX__Effort_Long, Effort_Medium, Effort_Fail, Spark_Launch, Scan_Loop_Play, Scan_Start, Scan_Stop and Scan_Single - now render audio instead of nothing.

Which half is the left channel is the one thing the bytes cannot say; the natural order is taken (channel 0 first), and swapping it would swap the stereo image of eight sound effects played through a mono speaker.

records.title: An action's track mask is a lock, taken while it runs
records.provenance: IActionRunner::Update and MovementComponent::LockTracks, read
evidence: Every action carries a track mask at +0x54. IActionRunner::Update 0x00540370 reads it and asks MovementComponent::AreAnyTracksLocked(mask) at 0x00540440: while any of those tracks is held it warns "Action %s [%d] not running because required tracks are locked" (0x005404A8) and does not run the action - it stays queued and is tried again on the next tick. Otherwise it locks them through the helper at 0x004F0F4C, which calls MovementComponent::LockTracks(mask, tag, name), and then runs the action.

LockTracks 0x00640098 walks the bits of the mask and inserts one LockInfo - the owner's name and reason - per track into a multiset at component+0x30; UnlockTracks 0x0063FE5C removes them. So a track is held by a set of owners and is free when the last one lets go.

The mask is therefore mutual exclusion, not muting: the animation plays its tracks and nothing else may drive them while it does. This stack claims the clip's tracks on the behaviour's scope and the scheduler refuses a play whose tracks are owned, which is the same arrangement; the refusal now waits and retries, as IActionRunner does, instead of treating the play as done.

The third argument of PlayTrigger was a suppressTracks mask whose note claimed the engine mutes a track for one play. It is now alsoLock, and it is added to the scope's claim: BehaviorReactToUnexpectedMovement's tracksToLock of 4 means the reaction holds the body track while it plays, which keeps the keep-alive and anything else off the wheels - not that the animation's own body track is silenced.

records.title: The sub-pixel corner refinement
records.effect: a refined corner lands in a slightly different place than the engine would put it, so the marker pose does too
records.provenance: CornerRefinement transcribes RefineCorners, ComputeBrightDarkValues and RefineQuadrilateral in single precision, and MarkerDetector now refines each quad against its homography before decoding it, as DetectFiducialMarkers does; the local edge-walk refinement is no longer used. The one part not transcribed instruction by instruction is Matrix::SolveLeastSquaresWithCholesky: this stack solves the same symmetric 8x8 normal equations by Cholesky decomposition and reports a non-positive pivot as the numerical failure
records.authority: VisionMarker::RefineCorners 0x0089FD98, VisionMarker::ComputeBrightDarkValues 0x0089F8E8, RefineQuadrilateral 0x008C55E0 and its corner helper 0x008C66C4, MarkerDetector::Parameters::Initialize 0x008752F8, DetectFiducialMarkers 0x00898760, read
evidence: Samples (0x008C570E..0x008C5C62): m = ceil(numSamples / 8) per edge block and eight blocks: outer edges y = 0 and 1 over x from the padding to 1 - padding, inner edges y = inner and 1 - inner over x from max(inner, padding), then the same for x; the template gradient is (0, -off), (0, +off), (0, +off), (0, -off) for the four x-running blocks and (-off, 0), (+off, 0), (+off, 0), (-off, 0) for the y-running ones, with the corner samples given the perpendicular gradient too when the padding is zero. off = (bright - dark) / 255 * 0.5 * (longer diagonal / sqrt 2) (0x008C583C..0x008C585E)
Jacobian (0x008C5CE6..0x008C5D86): the eight steepest-descent images Tx*x, Tx*y, Tx, Ty*x, Ty*y, Ty, -Tx*x*x - Ty*x*y, -Tx*x*y - Ty*y*y

Each iteration (0x008C5F3A..0x008C6192): every sample is mapped through the current homography; a sample whose floor or ceiling leaves the image is skipped; the image is read bilinearly at (u, v) from the four pixels at floor(u)..floor(u)+1, floor(v)..ceil(v); the error is (value - (bright + dark) / 2) / 255; J'J (upper triangle) and J'e are accumulated. Then MakeSymmetric, SolveLeastSquaresWithCholesky, the update [[1+d0, d1, d2], [d3, 1+d4, d5], [d6, d7, 1]] inverted by Invert3x3 and composed on the right, H = H * inv(U) (0x008C620A..0x008C629A), renormalised by H22 when |H22 - 1| >= 1e-5 (0x008C62A0..0x008C634A)

Stopping: the corners are recomputed from H for (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1) and the largest move taken (0x008C66C4); the loop ends when it is below minCornerChange, at the iteration limit, or on a numerical failure; a numerical failure puts back the initial quad and homography, otherwise the result is 1 when the corners moved more than maxCornerChange in all (0x008C63E4..0x008C6464)

RefineCorners 0x0089FD98: ComputeBrightDarkValues with minContrastRatio first (validity 2 when it fails), then RefineQuadrilateral with the dark level, the bright level, the iteration count, the sample count and the two change limits; a non-zero result is returned (the marker is then not decoded, validity 7 at 0x00899554); otherwise the refined corners rounded to s16 must pass IsQuadrilateralReasonable or the original corners are put back

records.title: The memory map's vision-derived content: the overhead edges
records.effect: none known
records.provenance: the detector, the chains and the four MapComponent entry points that turn them into map content are the engine's, with every constant read from it
records.authority: OverheadEdgesDetector::Detect 0x006ABE34, its construction in VisionSystem::VisionSystem 0x006B0120, GroundPlaneROI 0x004F7774 and its statics at 0x00C48F60, MapComponent::ProcessVisionOverheadEdges 0x0067F7AC, AddVisionOverheadEdges 0x0067F814, FlagQuadAsNotInterestingEdges 0x0067E6B0, FlagGroundPlaneROIInterestingEdgesAsUncertain 0x0067E50C with its lambda at 0x00680B54, MemoryMap::FillBorderInternal and QuadTreeProcessor::FillBorder 0x00689FAC, all read
evidence: The detector. GroundPlaneROI is the trapezoid its four statics describe, 40 to 190 mm ahead and 40 to 150 mm wide (0x00C48F60, GetGroundQuad 0x004F7774). Detect projects it, filters the bounding rectangle with the seven-by-five kernel at 0x00C8E020 (identical for the colour and grey paths), masks everything outside the quad away (fillConvexPoly of the quad's corners 0, 2, 3, 1 then SetMaskTo), transposes and walks each column from the bottom up for the first response past the threshold of 50 that VisionSystem constructs it with (0x006B0120). A column with none reports the far end clear, but only between the x of the quad's two far corners (0x006AD23E). Image points become ground points through the homography, refused when its third component is not positive (0x006AE0A8). The lift is a gate rather than a mask: unless the first of two points on it projects below the ROI rectangle, or the second above it, the frame is abandoned (0x006AC4A2..0x006ACDC8). Points join a chain while they are of the same kind and within 5 mm (0x006AE1B0).

The map side. AddVisionOverheadEdges puts each point in world coordinates through the robot's pose at the frame's timestamp, splits the ray at the ROI's near edge and asks HasCollisionRayWithTypes about each half with the two masks at 0x00C8768B and 0x00C876A1, and accumulates runs that hold their direction to within forty degrees (0.766 at 0x0067F980). A run longer than the noise length (the literal 6.00001 at 0x0067FA14) becomes the triangle between the robot and its ends as ClearOfObstacle, or a line to its midpoint when the run is under fifteen millimetres (225 as a squared length at 0x0067FF5C); a run from a border chain also goes in as a two-point InterestingEdge (the type byte 9 at 0x006802AC). Then the border pass, QuadTreeProcessor::FillBorder 0x00689FAC through RefreshBorderCombination: an interesting edge touching one of the masked types - the obstacles and NotInterestingEdge, the table at 0x00C87675 - is written off as NotInterestingEdge.

The two entry points the visit behaviour uses are in as well: FlagQuadAsNotInterestingEdges 0x0067E6B0 inserts the quad as type 10 with the last image's timestamp, and FlagGroundPlaneROIInterestingEdgesAsUncertain 0x0067E50C transforms the content inside the ROI with a lambda (0x00680B54) that turns type 9 into type 0 and leaves the rest alone.

Two differences, neither observable in what the map answers: the engine carries its regions in a quad tree subdivided to ten millimetres (GetContentPrecisionMM 0x00685000) and this keeps the polygons, which is the same difference M14-007 already records; and the filter response is computed here in double over one channel rather than in 16-bit over three, which moves no threshold decision that a marker-sized step would not pass either way.

records.title: The dark mask and the quad acceptance test are the engine's
records.provenance: ExtractComponentsViaCharacteristicScale_binomial, BinomialFilter, IsQuadrilateralReasonable and the parameters they are given, read
records.authority: ExtractComponentsViaCharacteristicScale_binomial 0x00890448, ImageProcessing::BinomialFilter 0x008A2344, IsQuadrilateralReasonable 0x00892B18, ComputeQuadrilateralsFromConnectedComponents 0x00892D70, MarkerDetector::Parameters::Initialize 0x008752F8 and the call in DetectFiducialMarkers at 0x00898C18, read
evidence: The dark test is a filtered value and a Q16 multiplier, not a fraction of a box mean. ExtractComponentsViaCharacteristicScale_binomial 0x00890448 runs one pass per pyramid level - DownsampleByTwo, BinomialFilter, |filtered - image| as the response (Matrix::Elementwise::ApplyOperation<SumOfAbsDiff> at 0x008907F4), UpsampleByPowerOfTwoBilinear back to full size - and its "ecvcsB_scale_select" loop at 0x00890B14 keeps the filtered value wherever the response beats the best so far. Its "ecvcsB_binarize" loop at 0x00890BB6 then marks a pixel dark when (scale * multiplier) >> 16 > pixel.

The two numbers come from the parameters DetectFiducialMarkers hands it at 0x00898C18: the word at +4 is the number of pyramid levels and Initialize sets it to 1 (0x0087530E), and the word at +0xC is the threshold multiplier, 0xCCCC (0x00875314), which is 0.79998779 in Q16. This stack had a three-level box pyramid and a local guess of 0.75.

BinomialFilter 0x008A2344 (coretech vision/robot/src/filtering.cpp) is the separable five-tap [1 4 6 4 1] with a >> 4 after each pass (the interior at 0x008A2490..0x008A24A6), and at the borders the off-image taps take the edge pixel: the first column's weights fold into 11, 4, 1 (0x008A243C) and the second's into 5, 6, 4, 1 (0x008A2458).

IsQuadrilateralReasonable 0x00892B18 is four tests in order: the cross product of the first three corners must reach quads_minQuadArea in absolute value (0x00892B5C), the cross products the diagonals make must agree in sign (0x00892C68, 0x00892CCA), one diagonal's two triangles must satisfy max << 8 < threshold * min (0x00892CFC..0x00892D22), and every corner must be at least the margin from each edge (0x00892D3A). ComputeQuadrilateralsFromConnectedComponents passes them from the parameters' +0x30, +0x34 and +0x38: 25, 512 - which is 2.0 in 8.8, not the maximum number of quads this stack had recorded - and 2.
The side-length floor this stack applied instead (six pixels, and a tenth of the longest side) is not in the engine's test and is gone.

The stricter mask moves the smallest marker the front end will take. Rendered squares are found down to twenty pixels a side and lost at sixteen, where the dark run falls under component_minimumNumPixels (100, the parameters' +0x4C); the looser local mask had been scraping past that floor. One navigation test had a cube at 400 mm, far enough that its marker is under the floor, and now stands it at 300.

Tracking happens inside CheckIfDone, which the action list calls every basestation tick; the constructor leaves the three times at +0xE4..+0xEC at -1 and the update timeout at +0x7C is not a period either. records.title: The memory map, and the question the face behaviour asks it before driving in
records.provenance: CanDriveIdealDistanceForward, TransitionToDrivingForward, the content-type table, the family mapping and the two insertion paths, read
records.authority: BehaviorInteractWithFaces::CanDriveIdealDistanceForward 0x005C2420, BehaviorInteractWithFaces::TransitionToDrivingForward 0x005C254E, MemoryMap::HasCollisionRayWithTypes 0x0068176E, ObjectFamilyToMemoryMapContentType 0x0067F4C0, MapComponent::AddObservableObject 0x0067ECFC, BlockWorld::AddMarkerlessObject 0x00622380, the EContentType names at 0x00BFFAC8 and the mask at 0x00C67962, read
evidence: The question is a ray. CanDriveIdealDistanceForward 0x005C2420 takes the local point (40, 0, 0) (0x42200000 at 0x005C2442), turns it by the robot's rotation, adds the robot's translation, and calls the memory map's virtual at +0x30 with the two x,y pairs and the type array at 0x00C67962, returning the negation (0x005C24A4). HasCollisionRayWithTypes 0x0068176E folds the array into a flag mask - EContentTypeToFlag for every entry whose bool is set - and hands it to the quad tree's ray walk.

The mask is eleven (type, bool) pairs: 00 00, 01 00, 02 00, 03 01, 04 01, 05 00, 06 01, 07 01, 08 01, 09 01, 0a 01. With the names from the table at 0x00BFFAC8 - Unknown, ClearOfObstacle, ClearOfCliff, ObstacleObservable, ObstacleCharger, ObstacleChargerRemoved, ObstacleProx, ObstacleUnrecognized, Cliff, InterestingEdge, NotInterestingEdge - everything blocks the drive except the first three and ObstacleChargerRemoved.

The answer changes the distance, not whether it drives. TransitionToDrivingForward loads -15.0 (vmov.f32 s0, #-15.0 at 0x005C2566) and replaces it with 40.0 only when the call returned true (0x005C2572), then builds DriveStraightAction(robot, distance, 40.0) - so a blocked robot backs off 15 mm. This stack drove 40 mm at 50 mm/s either way.

What goes in the map: MapComponent::AddObservableObject 0x0067ECFC inserts the object's bounding quad (its virtual GetBoundingQuadXY(pose, 0), vtable +0x50) with a MemoryMapData_ObservableObject, whose constructor 0x00684A38 stamps content type 3; ObjectFamilyToMemoryMapContentType 0x0067F4C0 is the tbb that decides it - Block, LightCube and CustomObject give ObstacleObservable on add and ClearOfObstacle on remove, the charger gives ObstacleCharger and ObstacleChargerRemoved, Ramp and Mat give Unknown, and a markerless object is refused with "ContentType MarkerlessObject addition is not supported". BlockWorld::AddMarkerlessObject 0x00622380 inserts a Cliff (type 8) for a CliffDetection object and a ProxObstacle (type 6) for a ProxObstacle one, and nothing for a CollisionObstacle (the type test at 0x0062259A falls through) - so the obstacle an unexpected movement leaves behind is in the world model and never in the map.

Implemented as Vision/MemoryMap.cs: the eleven content types, the family mapping, the mask, Insert, HasCollisionRayWithTypes and a sync that follows the world model's located objects, with the behaviour asking it before it drives. The engine keeps its regions in a quad tree (QuadTree 0x00684C08) subdivided to GetContentPrecisionMM; this keeps the polygons, which answers the same ray exactly rather than to the tree's precision. The map's vision-derived content - the overhead edges that become InterestingEdge and NotInterestingEdge, and the explored region the robot's own passage leaves - is M11-017.

records.title: Needs decay modifiers, damaged parts and persistence
records.provenance: NeedsState::GetDecayMultipliers, NumDamagedPartsForRepairLevel and the NeedsManager's device write, read, with the shipped configs
records.authority: NeedsState::GetDecayMultipliers 0x0069C214, NeedsState::NumDamagedPartsForRepairLevel 0x0069CCAC, NeedsManager::WriteToDevice 0x00693BB0 and NeedsFilenameFromSerialNumber 0x00695224, read
evidence: One need scales another's decay through an array of three multipliers. NeedsState::GetDecayMultipliers 0x0069C214 starts them at one and, for each need, takes its level and walks that need's modifier list: every entry whose threshold the level is at or under multiplies the listed other need's entry (the compare at 0x0069C270, the multiply and store at 0x0069C2A4). ApplyDecayAllNeeds 0x00695CFE asks for them once and passes the array to NeedsState::ApplyDecay, so the whole pass uses one set.

The shipped needs_decay_config.json carries ConnectedDecayModifiersEnergy and ConnectedDecayModifiersRepair. Every entry multiplies by one except Repair's at 0.03, which doubles Play: while Repair is at or below 0.03, Play decays twice as fast. That is the only modifier in the shipped data that changes anything.

Damaged parts follow the Repair level. NumDamagedPartsForRepairLevel 0x0069CCAC walks the broken-part thresholds in order and counts the leading run that is at or above the level, stopping at the first below it (0x0069CCC8). The thresholds are needs_config.json's BrokenPartThreshold0..2 - 0.98, 0.6 and 0.3 - so a full robot has none damaged, below 0.98 one, below 0.6 two and below 0.3 three. RepairRounds is 1. Which part is picked (PickPartToDamage 0x0069CCDE, PickPartToRepair 0x0069CD30) is cosmetic and is not modelled.

Persistence is per robot and carries a timestamp. NeedsFilenameFromSerialNumber 0x00695224 builds a prefix, an underscore (0x006952FC) and the serial with ".json" on the end; WriteToDevice 0x00693BB0 writes the levels with system_clock::now() divided by a million, that is whole seconds; and ApplyDecayForTimeSinceLastDeviceWrite 0x00695304 decays for the elapsed time when the file is read back, with InitAfterSerialNumberAcquired, StartReadFromRobot and InitAfterReadFromRobotAttempt ordering the startup. NeedsManager.Save and Load are that, with the path left to the host as the engine leaves it to the app.

records.title: The flat 3 s cooldown for an activity that ended as soon as it started
records.provenance: IActivityStrategy::WantsToStart and its call site, read
evidence: The two float arguments are the activity's own times, read together at the call site: ldrd r3, r2, [r1, #0x54] at 0x005B26FE gives r3 = +0x54 and r2 = +0x58, and WantsToStart measures the cooldown from the second (0x005B531C adds the cooldown to it) - so +0x58 is the last end time and +0x54 the last start.

Their difference is the length of the last run: s22 = arg2 - arg3 at 0x005B52EA. The engine asks BaseStationTimer::GetTimeSinceLastTickInSeconds (0x005B52F2), doubles it (0x005B5304), and when the run was positive but no longer than that - two ticks - it uses a flat 3 seconds (vmov.f32 s0, #3.0 at 0x005B5312) in place of the configured cooldown at +0x20.

The rest of the test is as recorded: no cooldown at all below the 1e-05 epsilon, no wait for an activity that has never ended unless startInCooldown is set (+0x28), and on passing, the cooldown is re-randomised as base (+0x1C) plus RandDbl(randomness at +0x24).
This stack now records the start time alongside the end time and applies the three seconds.

records.title: Activity deselection hook and the null-pick path
records.provenance: IActivity::OnDeselected, IActivity::GetDesiredActiveBehavior and ActivityFreeplay::GetDesiredActiveBehaviorInternal, read end to end
records.authority: IActivity::OnDeselected 0x005B33B8, IActivity::OnSelected 0x005B312C, IActivity::GetDesiredActiveBehavior 0x005B387C, ActivityFreeplay::GetDesiredActiveBehaviorInternal 0x005AE29C, ActivityFreeplay::PickNewActivityForSpark 0x005ADC44, SelectionBSRunnableChooser::OnDeselected 0x0060AF64, NeedsManager::SparksRewardCommunicatedToUser 0x00696E64, BehaviorEarnedSparks::StopInternal 0x005DAF70, read
evidence: The deselection hook is IActivity::OnDeselected 0x005B33B8, and it runs in this order: stamp the end time at +0x58 (OnSelected stamps the start at +0x54, 0x005B3142); call the chooser's hook, its vtable +0x24, of which only SelectionBSRunnableChooser::OnDeselected 0x0060AF64 does anything - it disables its selected behaviour's info-analyzer process, the mirror of OnSelected 0x0060AF20; remove the idle animation from the AnimationStreamer (robot+0x60) and the driving animations from the handler (robot+0x24c), each keyed by the activity's debug name and each only if the config named one (+0x44, +0x38 against 0x23f); drop the AIInformationAnalyzer enable request (+0x48); release every SmartDisableReactions lock in the set at +0x5c and destroy the set; SmartRemoveIdleAnimation if the pushed flag at +0x50 is set; clear the current-behaviour shared_ptr at +0x2c; and log robot.freeplay_goal_ended with the duration in whole seconds, a negative one raising "IActivity.Exit.NegativeDuration".

One thing in that list was missing here: if the needs manager still has a freeplay sparks reward pending (+0x3d8), OnDeselected calls NeedsManager::SparksRewardCommunicatedToUser (0x005B3548). That routine 0x00696E64 clears the flag and sends FreeplaySparksAwarded with the amount at +0x3dc. Its other two callers are BehaviorEarnedSparks::StopInternal 0x005DAF70 - which tests the byte and tail-calls it, so the reward is communicated when that behaviour *stops*, not when it starts, as this stack had it - and RegisterNeedsActionCompleted 0x006963C0, which sends a pending reward before creating a new one ("About to create freeplay sparks reward message but there was a pending one, so sending that one now").

The null-pick path is the second half of GetDesiredActiveBehaviorInternal 0x005AE29C. Before asking the activity it decides, in order: a debug-forced activity (+0x91) that is not the current one; the requested activity (+0x90) that is not the current one; a spark change or no current activity at all; then, only when no behaviour is running (0x005AE352) and no sparks reward is pending (0x005AE362), the strategy's WantsToEnd. Then it asks IActivity::GetDesiredActiveBehavior 0x005B387C and decides again on the answer: a null pick logs "ActivityFreeplay.ChooseNextBehavior.NoBehaviorChosenWhileRunning: Picking new activity because '%s' chose behavior '%s'. This activity is not allowed to be repicked." and jumps back to the pick with PickNewActivityForSpark's third argument false (0x005AE75C); a pick that is not the behaviour already running - IBehavior+0xa1, the flag Init sets (0x005BCD06) and Stop clears (0x005BD10C) - logs "NewBehaviorChosenWhileRunning" and jumps back with it true (0x005AE702), unless a sparks reward is pending. That third argument is read at 0x005ADCA2: the activity that is still current is only eligible again when it is passed true and its strategy does not want to end.

So an activity whose chooser yields nothing is dropped at once and barred from the re-pick, and an activity that wants to end survives only while the same behaviour keeps running - the moment its chooser would start a different one, the activity goes instead. This stack kept the activity and only stopped the unrunnable behaviour; the tick's middle is now the engine's loop.

records.title: The feature gate, and where boredomMultiplier is actually read
records.provenance: WantsToStart, CozmoFeatureGate and BehaviorPounceOnMotion, read, against the shipped configs
records.authority: IActivityStrategy::WantsToStart 0x005B529C, CozmoFeatureGate::IsFeatureEnabled 0x006A679C and BehaviorPounceOnMotion's constructor 0x005F7F91, read
evidence: The feature gate is the first thing WantsToStart tests: the flag at strategy+0x38 and then CozmoFeatureGate::IsFeatureEnabled(featureType), refusing outright when it says no (0x005B52A8..0x005B52BC). IsFeatureEnabled 0x006A679C turns the enum into its name, lowercases it and looks it up; the list comes from config/features.json, the path at 0x00BE8449. The shipped file has seventeen entries, with Invalid, SparksGatherCubes and Bouncer off and the rest on, and the only two activities that name a gate - singing.json and sparksCozmoSings.json - name Singing, which is on. This stack now parses featureGate and consults FeatureGates.

boredomMultiplier is not a scoring field at all. The string appears once in the whole binary, inside BehaviorPounceOnMotion's constructor (0x005F8384, among that class's own keys maxNoGroundMotionBeforeBored_* and maxTimeBehaviorTimeout_Sec), so the only reader is that behaviour, reading its own config. The one place the shipped data sets it is hiking.json's scoring block for Hiking_PounceOnMotion, which is an activity's scoring entry and never reaches the behaviour's config - neither pounceOnMotion config carries the key. So the value is dead data, and recording it without applying it is correct.

The pyramid strategy's 300 s cooldown (0x43960000) is already recorded; there is no separate random factor in it beyond the RandDbl(randomness) every strategy gets when its cooldown passes, which this stack applies in RandomizeCooldown.

records.title: The needsActionID hook and desired-from-objects ordering
records.provenance: CalculateDesiredActivityFromObjects, IBehavior::NeedActionCompleted, the two ExtractNeedsActionIDFromConfig routines and every call site, read
records.authority: ActivityFreeplay::CalculateDesiredActivityFromObjects 0x005ADF4C, IBehavior::NeedActionCompleted 0x005BE40C, IBehavior::IBehavior 0x005BBCAA, IBehavior::ExtractNeedsActionIDFromConfig 0x005BBAE8, IActivity::ReadConfig 0x005B2A9C, IActivity::ExtractNeedsActionIDFromConfig 0x005B3094, the sixteen NeedActionCompleted call sites and ActivityGatherCubes::Update 0x005AF2F0, read
evidence: The desired activity from what is around is a plain four-way switch. CalculateDesiredActivityFromObjects 0x005ADF4C takes the two booleans and reads the name at +0x68 for face and cube, +0x69 for a face alone, +0x6A for a cube alone and +0x6B for neither, storing the pick at +0x90. That is the order DesiredActivityNames carries here - faceAndCube, faceOnly, cubeOnly, noFaceNoCube - and DesiredActivityFromObjects already matched it.

The needs-action hook belongs to the behaviour, not the activity. IBehavior::NeedActionCompleted 0x005BE40C is four instructions: when the caller passes Invalid the behaviour's own id at +0x68 is used (the cbnz at 0x005BE40C), and the result goes to NeedsManager::RegisterNeedsActionCompleted through the robot. IBehavior's constructor fills +0x68 at 0x005BBCAA from ExtractNeedsActionIDFromConfig 0x005BBAE8, which reads the config's needsActionID string and converts it; twenty-two shipped behaviour configs carry the key.

Sixteen behaviours call it. Ten pass Invalid and so report their own configured action - KnockOverCubes at TransitionToPlayingReaction but only when the stack came apart (the flag at +0x14c gates the objective and the report together, 0x005C3950), PopAWheelie on the docking success beside objective PoppedWheelie (0x005C7E14), RollBlock::TransitionToRollSuccess, StackBlocks::TransitionToPlayingFinalAnim, CubeLiftWorkout::EndIteration, BuildPyramid::TransitionToReactingToPyramid, FistBump::UpdateInternal, PeekABoo::TransitionExit, TrackLaser::StopInternal and the singing behaviour's last step, which falls back to CozmoSings when its config has none (0x005EF7CA). Six name one outright: PickupCube 0x1F from BehaviorExploreBringCubeToBeacon::TransitionToObjectPickedUp, StackCube 0x2A from the explorer's stacking callback (0x005E14B6), GuardDogLose/Win/NoInteraction 0x15/0x16/0x17 from BehaviorGuardDog::RecordResult, PlacedOnSide 0x2F and BoredOnSide 0x30 from BehaviorReactToRobotOnSide, and DizzyMedium/DizzySoft 0x0F/0x10 from BehaviorReactToRobotShaken. One activity reports directly to the manager: ActivityGatherCubes::Update passes GatherCubes 0x14 when every cube is in a beacon (0x005AF2F0). The enum names come from the EnumToString table at 0x01033D40, 0x57 entries.

An activity's own needsActionID is dead data. IActivity::ReadConfig stores it at IActivity+0x1C (0x005B2A9C) and nothing loads that word again: no IActivity or Activity* method reads +0x1C on the activity, and the one activity that reports an action names it itself. So the three shipped activity-level ids - PyramidCompleted, PyramidCompleted_Sparked, CozmoSingsCompleted_Sparked - are never reported, and neither is the pyramid behaviour's, since no pyramid behaviour config carries the key. This stack reported the activity's id when the activity ended; that call is gone, and the behaviours report their own through BehaviorNeedsActions.

records.title: The beacon is centred on the robot
records.provenance: BehaviorThinkAboutBeacons::SelectNewBeacon, read
evidence: SelectNewBeacon 0x005E5F0C is four calls: it takes the AIWhiteboard from the AI component at Robot+0x264, asks the robot for its pose (0x005E5F1A, which reads Robot+0x298), copies that pose into a local (0x005E5F24), and calls AIWhiteboard::AddBeacon(pose, radius) with the float the behaviour keeps at +0x128 from its config (0x005E5F28).

So the centre is the robot's pose at the moment the beacon is placed and the radius is the configured one - which is what this stack does. AddBeacon 0x0056C39C is the only caller of the whiteboard's beacon list, so no other centre is ever chosen.

records.title: The block pool is kept in blockPool.txt between sessions, and an RSSI tie is broken in the engine container order
evidence: Robot::SetPhysicalRobot(true) 0x00513914 calls BlockFilter::Init 0x0061A1EC with DataPlatform::pathToResource(scope 4, "blockPool.txt") (0x0051394C, the string at 0x005139B0); Robot::Robot only constructs the filter (0x00510184). Init stores the path at +0x60, calls Load, copies the persistent pool (+0x04) to the runtime pool (+0x2C) and calls Robot::ConnectToObjects with its five factory ids (0x0061A278) - before any BlockPoolEnabledMessage. This stack calls Init from CozmoRobot.ConnectAsync with a file under the local application data folder, the platform's equivalent of that data scope; an empty path turns persistence off

Load 0x0061A2DC: ifstream(path, in); a file that will not open leaves the pool as it is. getline on '\n'; an empty line is skipped; a sixth non-empty line is an error that ends the reading (0x0061A41E, sErrorF at 0x0061A5A0); a line whose first two characters are not "0x" is skipped (compare at 0x0061A430); id = stoul(line, &pos, 16) (0x0061A442), skipped when pos reaches the end of the line, stored in the next entry, then type = stoul(line.substr(pos + 1), 0, 10) (0x0061A480) stored beside it and the entry counted. A throwing stoul is caught, logged and the line skipped (0x0061A52C..0x0061A58E) - after the id has been stored when it is the type that fails

Save 0x0061B014: nothing without a path; when all five ids are zero an existing file is removed (stat, remove at 0x0061B058..0x0061B068); then ofstream(path, out) and, for each entry with a non-zero id, "0x" (0x0061B344), the id in hex (basefield cleared to hex at 0x0061B0FE..0x0061B102, lower case), "," (0x0061B348), to_string(type) and "\n" (0x0061B34C). Save is called by AddObjectToPersistentPool on success (0x0061ACE2), RemoveObjectFromPersistentPool (0x0061B410) and the game's block-pool messages in HandleGameEvents (0x00619FC0, 0x0061A0A6, 0x0061A10E); only the first path exists in this stack

The table at Robot+0x47C is std::__ndk1::unordered_map<unsigned, Robot::ActiveObjectInfo> with std::hash<unsigned>, the key its own hash. operator[] 0x00537ABC: bucket = h & (n-1) for a power-of-two count, h % n otherwise; a new key first grows the table when it is empty or n * max_load_factor < size + 1 to max((2n) | (n < 3 || n not a power of two), ceil((size + 1) / mlf)) (0x00537B2C..0x00537B90); rehash 0x00537C80 turns 1 into 2 and a non-power-of-two into __next_prime, so the counts run 2, 5, 11, 23; the node goes after its bucket's head when the bucket is in use, else at the front of the list with the bucket pointing at the list head and the displaced node's bucket at the new node (0x00537BAE..0x00537BF8); __rehash 0x00537D10 rebuilds by walking the list and splicing each node into an in-use bucket after its head; erase (remove 0x00518FDA) unlinks and repairs the bucket pointers

GetClosestDiscoveredObjectsOfType 0x00518314 walks that table in its iteration order and takes a later entry at an equal RSSI byte, so a tie goes to the entry the container visits last. The order is incidental to the container, but it is fully determined by the insertion and erase history, which this stack sees identically (advertisements, the 10001 ms timeout, connections), so it is reproduced exactly by ActiveObjectTable rather than approximated

records.title: The complete live-animation wire lifecycle
records.effect: live keyframes (idle body, head, lift, face) start, interleave with a streamed animation, or stop on the wire differently from the engine
records.provenance: once the live stream is active it is streamed on every tick in which no clip runs: opened with one audio silence and StartOfAnimation tag 0xFF, then one audio silence per frame within the robot's audio budget, the live keyframes appended into it; a clip taking over ends it without an EndOfAnimation and the next tick after the clip reopens it. The stream becomes active at the first live keyframe, which is when this stack's idle behaviour starts, rather than at engine start; and a tick streams one frame where the engine streams to its budget - the same frames on the wire at the same cadence
records.authority: AnimationStreamer::UpdateLiveAnimation 0x0057D5F8, AnimationStreamer::Update 0x0057CE5C, InitStream 0x0057B674, UpdateStream 0x0057C84C, SendStartOfAnimation 0x0057C400, SendBufferedMessages 0x0057BF60, read
evidence: UpdateLiveAnimation 0x0057D5F8 sends nothing itself: it appends HeadAngle, BodyMotion and LiftHeight keyframes to the live Animation (AddKeyFrameToBack at 0x0057D866, 0x0057D8F4, 0x0057D9CA)

Update 0x0057CE5C, with no streaming animation: sets the idle animation to the live one at this+0xA8 (0x0057D070..0x0057D07C), calls UpdateLiveAnimation (0x0057D080), and when the live animation is not already the one streaming calls InitStream(live, 0xFF) (movs r2, #0xff; 0x0057D3FC..0x0057D3FE), otherwise UpdateStream(live) (0x0057D430) - every update

InitStream 0x0057B674 stores the tag at this+0xA0 (0x0057B68E), clears the send buffer (0x0057B7CE), sets endSent-suppression this+0x72 from Animation::IsEmpty (0x0057B7D8) and clears startSent this+0x71 (0x0057B7E2); it sends nothing, and it does not end the previous animation

UpdateStream 0x0057C84C, per frame: an AudioSample or AudioSilence is buffered first (0x0057C9A8 / 0x0057C9C4), then SendStartOfAnimation once when this+0x71 is clear (0x0057C9C8..0x0057C9D0; SendStartOfAnimation 0x0057C400 buffers StartOfAnimation with the tag at this+0xA0), then head, lift, event, face, procedural face, backpack lights, body (0x0057CA4E..0x0057CA56), record heading, turn to recorded heading, then SendBufferedMessages (0x0057CA82)

the live animation is empty when InitStream runs, so this+0x72 is set and the UpdateStream end path (0x0057CB64..0x0057CB6C) and the Update end path (0x0057D1D0..0x0057D1D6) never send its EndOfAnimation: the live stream stays open until another animation's InitStream replaces it

SendBufferedMessages 0x0057BF60 sends each buffered message reliably (Robot::SendMessage(msg, true, false) at 0x0057BFAA) within the byte budget at this+0x98 and counts tags 0x8E/0x8F ((tag & 0xFE) == 0x8E at 0x0057BF8C) against the budget at this+0x9C computed by UpdateAmountToSend 0x0057C6F0

Whether the robot requires StartOfAnimation or the audio framing to execute a body keyframe is firmware behaviour and is not answered by the engine; what the engine establishes is that it never sends a live keyframe outside a StartOfAnimation-opened, audio-framed stream. CR1's zero wheel movement is not explained by this reading

records.title: Knock over a stack: BehaviorKnockOverCubes has no verified fidelity record
records.effect: the approach, the flip of the bottom block, the blind-flip fallback or the success and failure reactions differ from the engine
records.provenance: the behaviour's flow is the engine's (see the evidence). DriveAndFlipBlockAction now takes the maximum face-turn angle and, when it is above zero, turns towards the last observed face after the drive with the result ignored, through this stack's TurnTowardsFaceAction for the last face where the engine constructs a TurnTowardsLastFacePoseAction; with no face detector (M11-016) there is no face and the turn does nothing. The AI whiteboard's +0x70 now feeds the NoPreDockPoses reaction, which targets RamIntoBlock
records.authority: BehaviorKnockOverCubes 0x005C2EA0..0x005C3C00, its knock-over callback 0x005C3DCE, IBehavior::StartActing(action, function<void(Robot&)>) 0x005BE0E4 and its lambda 0x005BF8F4, IBehavior::Init 0x005BCB54 and ReadFromJson 0x005BBFB4, read; DriveAndFlipBlockAction 0x0055E208 not read past its arguments; DriveAndFlipBlockAction 0x0055E208, IDriveToInteractWithObject 0x0055B1F4, ReactionTriggerStrategyNoPreDockPoses::ShouldTriggerBehaviorInternal 0x00610E32, AIWhiteboard::AIWhiteboard 0x0056A270 and BehaviorRamIntoBlock's transitions, read
evidence: InitInternal 0x005C31A2 goes straight to the knock-over when IBehavior+0xD9 (alwaysStreamline, ReadFromJson 0x005BC216) or +0xD8 (set in IBehavior::Init 0x005BCCC2 from the spark state) is set; neither shipped config sets alwaysStreamline and freeplay is not sparked, so the reach runs

Reach 0x005C3254: TurnTowardsObjectAction(max pi) at the bottom block; then, only when the block's x in the robot frame plus 10 exceeds 85 (0x005C3354..0x005C336C), DriveStraightAction(x - 85) at 60 mm/s; then the reachForBlockTrigger lift-safe animation. The continuation TransitionToKnockingOverStack runs whatever the result (StartActing's lambda 0x005BF8F4 ignores it)

Knock-over 0x005C34A8: a sequence of TurnTowardsObjectAction(max pi), DriveAndFlipBlockAction and WaitAction(0.5). The callback 0x005C3DCE: NoPreActionPoses (0x03000010) writes the block to AIWhiteboard+0x70 and ends; success goes to TransitionToPlayingReaction; a Retry-category result re-runs the knock-over while the attempt count at +0x140 is at most 1 and otherwise goes to the blind flip, counting up either way; anything else ends. The count is zeroed in InitializeMemberVars (0x005C3218)
Blind flip 0x005C3840: FlipBlockAction with the pre-action check off and WaitAction(0.5), then the reaction

DriveAndFlipBlockAction is constructed with useApproachAngle false, approach angle 0, sayName false, a maximum turn towards a face of pi/2 on the first attempt and 0 on later ones or when streamlined (the table at 0x005C36BC), false, and a trailing float of 20.0 (0x005C352E..0x005C3548), with the say-name triggers 0xFD and 0xFE

DriveAndFlipBlockAction(Robot&, ObjectID, bool useApproachAngle, float approachAngle, bool sayName, Radians maxTurnTowardsFaceAngle, bool, float) 0x0055E208 hands its stack arguments +0x70..+0x7C to IDriveToInteractWithObject (0x0055E22C..0x0055E24C) and never reads the trailing float at +0x80: the 20.0 KnockOverCubes passes has no effect

IDriveToInteractWithObject 0x0055B1F4: after the DriveToObjectAction sequence, when maxTurnTowardsFaceAngle > Radians(0) (0x0055B37C..0x0055B392) it adds a TurnTowardsLastFacePoseAction(face 0, that angle, sayName) with its failure ignored (AddAction(action, true) at 0x0055B3D4); at 0 it adds nothing. KnockOverCubes passes pi/2 on the first attempt and 0 once its attempt count is above zero, with sayName false

AIWhiteboard+0x70 is initialised to -1 in the constructor (0x0056A2E2) and not reset on delocalisation (OnRobotDelocalized 0x0056A686 does not touch it). Its only reader is ReactionTriggerStrategyNoPreDockPoses::ShouldTriggerBehaviorInternal 0x00610E32: finds RamIntoBlock (behaviour id 0x3C, 0x00610E4C); when +0x70 is not -1 it writes -1 back (0x00610E60), puts the object in RamIntoBlock+0x11C (0x00610E64) and triggers if the behaviour is runnable (0x00610E6C) - the reset preceding the test, so an object is consumed either way

RamIntoBlock+0x11C is the target every transition reads (TransitionToPuttingDownBlock 0x0060479C, TransitionToTurningToBlock 0x006048E8, TransitionToRammingIntoBlock 0x00604A4C) and StopInternal resets it (0x00604994).
